title: Stock vibe app
body:
Here's a stock vibe app I've been working on and deployed.

The main purpose originally was to have a command line tool with daily and weekly momentum outputs that I could run through my Alpaca paper account. Basically programmatic trading for myself. I can go more into that separately but if I ever make that public it'd become a whole product.

So this is somewhere between command line terminal and full useful product.

https://poetic-pastelito-638f2a.netlify.app/

Any secret sauce lives in the business logic. Also haven't added all the tricks, i.e. the longer I've traded short term, the more I believe volume is basically the main thing to scalp.

Appreciate any comments. Happy to help with technical problems. Not financial advice.

title: Good read
body:
Fun read. Got some ideas for some algos I've been testing (mostly just in TradingView (Pine)) as indicators and strategies, and for backtests. Specifically LPPL (or LPPLS) for usage as a "risk" oscillator that, when tweaked and tied to other indicators, at least gives a winning strategy (though not market beating over short timespans).

Interesting stuff.

title: LPPLS
body:
Follow up from previous post, testing LPPLS as an oscillator, and as a strategy. It's a pretty simple buy / sell strategy that definitely needs some work but shows how it can at least be profitable.

If you look closely and long enough, you start to get a feel for which way a quake will break based on the last risk indicator. Think of the triangles loosely as buy / sell indicators but it's not quite that straightforward.

I think it really only makes sense as a highly leveraged bet around the "earthquakes" themselves, with the oscillator potentially providing a clue as to which way the earthquake would pan out. So not a super long term strategy where you just start with $10k and win over hundreds of trades (won't beat the market), but a once a quarter type trade that generates an outsized return (up or down, doesn't matter, leverage and go for it calls / puts).

It's at least captivating.
